name: Question 41
problem:
$$
X=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 3 \\ 4 & 6 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the observation matrix $X$ above, where the individual observations are given in columns. Find the sample covariance matrix of the data.
worked_solution:
Recall that  the sample covariance matrix is given by

$$
C=\frac{1}{n-1}B{B}^{T},
$$

where $B$ is the observation matrix in the mean-deviation form, and $n$ is the number of observations.

So, we first need to compute the mean-deviation form of our observation matrix.

The sample mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{1}{3}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & ={x}_{1}-m=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {b}_{2} & ={x}_{2}-m=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {b}_{3} & ={x}_{3}-m=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the mean-deviation form is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the sample covariance matrix is 

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =\frac{1}{3-1}[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Recall that the sample covariance matrix is given by

C=1n−1BBT,

where B is the observation matrix in the mean-deviation form, and n is the number of observations.

So, we first need to compute the mean-deviation form of our observation matrix.

The sample mean is

m=13(x1+x2+x3)=13([24]+[16]+[35])=13[615]=[25].

Now, we have the following:

b1=x1−m=[24]−[25]=[0−1]b2=x2−m=[16]−[25]=[−11]b3=x3−m=[35]−[25]=[10]

Therefore, the mean-deviation form is

B=[0−11−110].

Finally, the sample covariance matrix is

C=13−1[0−11−110][0−1−1110]=12[2−1−12].
